title: Incremental Prometheus snapshot/restore + Helm precheck for private cluster upgrades
author: Priya Sharma
release_notes: Add an incremental Prometheus snapshot & restore operator plus a Helm preflight check for observability components to reduce downtime during private-cluster upgrades. Backward compatible; optional feature gated behind installer flag.
description:
Motivation: private installs observed significant Prometheus downtime during control-plane upgrades in customers with large TSDBs. Existing solutions (full snapshot + restore or blue/green shims) are heavy and error-prone in air-gapped environments. This PR introduces an incremental snapshot-and-restore flow for Prometheus plus Helm prechecks to avoid stateful data-loss and reduce manual intervention.

What this PR does: Adds a small controller (implemented as a Kubernetes Job + helper scripts deployed via Helm hooks) to take incremental TSDB snapshots before an upgrade, push artifacts to the configured object store (S3/GCS-compatible or local blob store), and perform a validated restore to a warm replica if the primary fails during the upgrade. Introduces a Helm precheck job that runs before observable upgrades to validate storage access, retention settings, WAL size heuristics, and available disk. Adds a terraform variable and installer flag (observability.incremental_prom_snapshot = true) to enable the flow for customers who opt-in.

High level components changed: 1) Helm charts: new charts/observability/operators/prom-snap-operator with preinstall/postupgrade hooks; 2) Installer: terraform/modules/observability/main.tf adds blobstore credentials and lifecycle-managed bucket creation when available; 3) Documentation: docs/observability/upgrade-playbooks.md with step-by-step runbooks and failure modes; 4) CI: test/integration/observability/upgrade-sim.sh to validate snapshot/restore in CI; 5) RBAC: minimal serviceaccount/rolebinding for operator jobs.

Design notes: - Incremental snapshots rely on Prometheus TSDB snapshot plus WAL segment copy for faster restores. We prefer incremental when bucket storage and retention are configured. - The operator is intentionally transient: it runs as a Job and cleans up snapshots > configurable retention. No long-lived controller required to keep the installer footprint small. - Helm prechecks fail fast (non-blocking when flag disabled). For air-gapped installs the precheck also validates local blobstore endpoints and certificate trust.

Backwards compatibility & opt-in: The flow is opt-in and defaults to false. Without the flag, installer behavior is unchanged. The Helm charts include templates that are no-ops unless the flag is set.

Testing performed: - Local integration: simulated 3-node Prometheus cluster; performed incremental snapshots and validated WAL re-attach and TSDB consistency after restore. - CI: added upgrade-sim.sh that runs in k8s-in-docker runner to exercise prechecks and snapshot/restore. - Tested with a mocked S3 endpoint to ensure airgapped TLS behavior is respected.

Operational runbook summary (also in docs): 1) Enable flag and run terraform apply. 2) Initiate upgrade; Helm precheck runs automatically. 3) If precheck passes, snapshot job runs and uploads incremental artifacts. 4) During upgrade, if the primary becomes unhealthy, operator triggers restore to warm replica. 5) After rollout, snapshots older than retention are garbage-collected.

Security considerations: credentials for blobstore are provisioned via installer secrets and never logged. Jobs run with minimal RBAC. Snapshots are encrypted at rest when the target supports server-side encryption.

Why this is unique: focuses on incremental (not full) snapshots, minimal transient operator, and explicit Helm precheck integration to reduce upgrade blast radius for private clusters where manual operator interventions are hard.

commits: 3 commits: 1) Add prom-snap-operator Helm chart + scripts (prom-snap-operator/). 2) Terraform: observer module flag and blobstore wiring. 3) Docs + test harness for upgrade simulation.
review_conversation: Ethan Blake: Please split the precheck into a small script and move heavy validation to optional mode; installer runs must stay fast.

Priya Sharma: Done. Precheck now has a fast 'core' mode that runs by default and a deferred 'deep' check you can enable separately. I split the script under charts/observability/precheck/ and added a timeout to the helm hook.
Marta Lindqvist: How do we handle partial uploads if connection drops? We need idempotency or resume support.

Priya Sharma: The upload uses an idempotent artifact key (cluster/tsdb/incremental/<snapshot-id>). A partial multipart upload is aborted and retried by the job; we added exponential backoff and a final integrity check (size + md5).
Tao Chen: CI flaked once on restore; I saw a race between job cleanup and restore attach.
Priya Sharma: Fixed by adding a lock file and a small wait loop in the restore script; retest shows stable behavior. Added an integration test to reproduce the race in CI.
Ethan Blake: Approving after minor nit fixes were applied.
Marta Lindqvist: Approved (tested locally with mocked S3).
Tao Chen: Approved and verified helm hook ordering is correct for upgrades.
ci_summary: Checks: lint (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass), e2e (pass after rerun). One flaky CI job (integration/upgrade-sim) failed on first run due to race; rerun passed.

Add monitoring alert for failed snapshot uploads to SRE alerting policy
notes_for_ops: If a restore fails, run docs/observability/upgrade-playbooks.md -> manual-restore section. For customers without blobstore, use local NFS endpoint; precheck validates NFS mountpoints.
risk_assessment: Low/Medium: new jobs run transiently. Opt-in by default. The only risk is misconfigured storage credentials which precheck will catch; mitigation documented.
estimated_rollout_time: 10-30 minutes per tenant (mostly precheck + snapshot upload latency)
